extracted.intended_audience: selective service administrators, registrants, employers, military and legal officials, and courts
extracted.subtask_description: Implementation and enforcement rules of the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940: registration, selection, exemptions, deferments, quotas, administrative structure, penalties, pay, re-employment and related procedural provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial selection for induction
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection of men for training and service shall be made in an impartial manner under such rules and regulations as the President may prescribe, from men liable for such training and service who at the time of selection are registered and classified but not deferred or exempted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 4(A) — selection must follow Presidential rules; applies to those registered/classified and not deferred/exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: No discrimination on race or color
rubrics_metrics.description: In the selection and training of men under this act, and in the interpretation and execution of the provisions of this act, there shall be no discrimination against any person on account of race or color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 4(A) — explicit nondiscrimination requirement governing all selection/training/administration under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-and-subdivision quota determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotas of men to be inducted shall be determined for each state, territory and the District of Columbia, and for subdivisions thereof, on the basis of the actual number of men in the several states, territories and the District of Columbia, and the subdivisions thereof, who are liable for such training and service but who are not deferred after classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 4(B) — credits for residents already in land/naval forces, estimates may be used until actual numbers known, subsequent adjustments required; computations per Presidential rules and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credits for residents already in forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Credits shall be given in fixing and filling such quotas for residents of subdivisions who are in the land and naval forces of the United States on the date fixed for determining such quotas and for those who subsequently become members of such forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 4(B) — quotas account for residents already serving; ensures fair quota filling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of estimates pending actual numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Until the actual numbers necessary for determining the quotas are known, the quotas may be based on estimates, and subsequent adjustments therein shall be made when such actual numbers are known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 4(B) — temporary quota-setting by estimate permitted; adjustments mandatory later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories not required to register (broad list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioned officers, warrant officers, pay clerks, and enlisted men of the Regular Army, the Navy, the Marine Corps, the Coast Guard, the Coast and Geodetic Survey, the Public Health Service, recognized active Officers’ Reserve Corps, the Regular Army Reserve, enlisted Reserve Corps, the Naval Reserve, the Marine Corps Reserve; cadets and midshipmen of the US Military, Naval and Coast Guard Academies; accepted cadets for imminent admission; advanced-course ROTC/NROTC cadets; and certain diplomatic and consular foreign representatives residing in the United States who are not citizens shall not be required to be registered under Section 2 and shall be relieved from liability for training and service under Section 3(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 5(A) — long enumerated list of personnel categories exempt from registration and liability; exemption applies while the listed status continues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — 3 years Regular Army service
rubrics_metrics.description: Any man who shall have satisfactorily served for at least three consecutive years in the Regular Army before or after or partially before and partially after the time fixed for registration under Section 2 shall be relieved from liability to serve in any reserve component and from liability for training and service under Section 3(B) in time of peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 5(B)(1) — prior consecutive Regular Army service of three years qualifies for exemption in peacetime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — National Guard plus Regular Army service pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Any man who as a member of the active National Guard shall have satisfactorily served for at least one year in active Federal service in the Army of the United States, and subsequent thereto for at least two consecutive years in the Regular Army or in the active National Guard, before or after or partially before and partially after the time fixed for registration under Section 2, shall be relieved from liability in time of peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 5(B)(2) — specific combined service pattern in Guard and Regular Army qualifies for exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — six consecutive years in active National Guard
rubrics_metrics.description: Any man who is in the active National Guard at the time fixed for registration under Section 2, and who shall have satisfactorily served therein for at least six consecutive years, before or after or partially before and partially after the time fixed for such registration, shall be relieved from liability in time of peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 5(B)(3) — sustained Guard service alone (6 years) qualifies for exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — six consecutive years on Officers’ Reserve eligible list
rubrics_metrics.description: Any man who is in the Officers’ Reserve Corps on the eligible list at the time fixed for registration under Section 2, and who shall have satisfactorily served on the eligible list for at least six consecutive years, shall be relieved from liability in time of peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 5(B)(4) — long-term officers’ reserve eligible-list service qualifies for exemption; does not prevent being ordered to active duty while in reserve components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferment while holding certain civil offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Vice-President, Governors, members of legislative bodies of the United States and of the several states and territories, judges of the courts of record of the United States and of the several states and territories and the District of Columbia shall, while holding such offices, be deferred from training and service under this act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 5(C)(1) — automatic deferment for listed civil officeholders for duration of office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential authority to defer for public health/safety/interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is authorized, under such rules and regulations as he may prescribe, to provide for the deferment from training and service of any person holding an office (other than those specifically listed) under the United States or any state, territory, or the District of Columbia, whose continued service in such office is found to be necessary to the maintenance of the public health, safety, or interest in accordance with Section 10(A)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 5(C)(2) and repeated in Sec. 5(E) — Presidential discretionary deferment where continuation in an office is necessary for public welfare; implemented by rules/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — ministers of religion and theological students
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular or duly ordained ministers of religion and students preparing for the ministry in theological or divinity schools recognized as such for more than one year prior to the date of enactment shall be exempt from training and service but not from registration under this act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 5(D) — religious ministry status and long-enrolled theological students exempt from service (must still register).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential deferment for employment necessary to national interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The President may provide for deferment from training and service of those men whose employment in industry, agriculture, or other occupations, or whose activity in other endeavors, is found in accordance with Section 10(A)(2) to be necessary to the maintenance of the national health, safety, or interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 5(E) — deferments allowed for critical civilian employment/activities by Presidential rule, using standards set in Sec.10(A)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential authority to defer for dependents and for persons found deficient
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is authorized to provide for deferment (1) of those men in respect to persons dependent upon them for which deferment is advisable, and (2) of those men found to be physically, mentally, or morally deficient or defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 5(E) — two further categories for Presidential deferment: dependent-family considerations and individual physical/mental/moral findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized deferment determinations; no group occupational deferments
rubrics_metrics.description: No deferment shall be made in the case of any individual except upon the determination of the status of such individual, and no such deferment shall be made of individuals by occupational groups or of groups of individuals in any plant or institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 5(E) — forbids blanket occupational or plant-wide deferments; requires individual determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conscientious objector process and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: A person conscientiously opposed to participation in combatant service may, in lieu of induction, be assigned to work of national importance under civilian direction; claims undergo hearing, Department of Justice recommendation, appeal to appeal board which gives consideration but is not bound by DOJ recommendation; those sustained are listed on a register of conscientious objectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text describes hearing, recommendation, appeal procedures and maintenance of a register; appeal board has final say subject to procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expiration of exceptions, exemptions, deferments when cause ceases
rubrics_metrics.description: No exception from registration, or exemption or deferment from training and service, under this act shall continue after the cause therefor ceases to exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 5(H) — conditional status ends when underlying justification no longer applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induction limited by Congressional appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: The President shall have authority to induct into the land and naval forces under this act no greater number of men than the Congress shall hereafter make specific appropriation for from time to time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 6 — induction numbers constrained by appropriations; Presidential authority subject to funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on bounties and substitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: No bounty shall be paid to induce any person to enlist in or be inducted; clothing or enlistment allowances authorized by law are not considered bounties; no person liable shall be permitted to furnish a substitute or escape service by payment of money or other valuable thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 7 — bars pecuniary substitutes or bounties as means to avoid induction; existing lawful allowances unaffected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates and medical statements upon completion of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person inducted who satisfactorily completes his period of training and service shall be entitled to a certificate which shall include a record of any special proficiency or merit; inducted persons shall be given a physical examination at beginning and completion of service and a medical statement showing defects, injuries, illnesses or disabilities noted or suffered during such period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 8(A) — documents evidencing completion and medical condition; certificates required for reemployment protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-employment rights after training/service — federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: If such position was in the employ of the United States government, its territories or possessions, or the District of Columbia, such person shall be restored to such position or to a position of like seniority, status and pay upon application within forty days after relief from training and service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 8(B)(a) — restoration to federal positions with like seniority/status/pay; timely application required (within 40 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-employment rights after training/service — private employers
rubrics_metrics.description: If such position was in the employ of a private employer, such employer shall restore such person to such position or to a position of like seniority, status and pay unless the employer’s circumstances have so changed as to make it impossible or unreasonable to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 8(B)(b) — private employers must re-employ unless circumstances make it impossible/unreasonable; employee must meet (1) have certificate, (2) be still qualified, (3) apply within 40 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-employment rights after training/service — state/local positions (sense of Congress)
rubrics_metrics.description: If such position was in the employ of any state or political subdivision thereof, it is the sense of Congress that such person should be restored to such position or to a position of like seniority, status and pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 8(B)(c) — moral/policy statement encouraging state/local restoration (not a direct federal mandate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of seniority, benefits, and one-year discharge protection
rubrics_metrics.description: A person restored to a position shall be considered as having been on furlough or leave of absence, shall be restored without loss of seniority, entitled to participate in insurance or other benefits offered by the employer pursuant to established rules, and shall not be discharged from such position without cause within one year after such restoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 8(C) — restoration preserves employment rights, benefits and provides one-year protection from dismissal without cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal remedies for private employer noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If any private employer fails or refuses to comply with re-employment provisions, the U.S. District Court for the district where the employer does business has power to require compliance and to compensate the person for any loss of wages or benefits; the court shall order a speedy hearing and may advance it on the calendar; the U.S. District Attorney may act as attorney for the claimant upon application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 8(E) — judicial enforcement mechanism; compensation and expedited proceedings; limitation that no fees or court costs shall be taxed against persons applying (text indicates protection from costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective service personnel division to aid re-employment
rubrics_metrics.description: The director of selective service shall establish a personnel division with adequate facilities to render aid in the replacement in their former positions of, or in securing positions for, members of the reserve components and persons who have satisfactorily completed any period of active duty or training and service under this act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 8(G) — administrative assistance to veterans/inductees seeking reemployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting rights while inducted
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person inducted shall, during the period of such training and service, be permitted to vote in person or by absentee ballot in any general, special, or primary election occurring in the state of which he is a resident, whether he is within or outside of such state at the time of such election, if under the laws of such state he is entitled so to vote; nothing requires granting leave longer than one day to permit in-person voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 8(H) — preserves franchise during service; limits employer obligation for time off to vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy discouraging replacement of inducted workers by subversive organization members
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the expressed policy of Congress that whenever a vacancy is caused in employment by induction, such vacancy shall not be filled by any person who is a member of the Communist party or the German-American Bund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 8 — policy statement; not presented as an enforceable statutory bar to hiring but as expressed policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential procurement authority and mandatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The President, through War or Navy Departments, may place orders with any individual/firm/industry for products or material required and usually produced by such entities; compliance with such orders shall be obligatory and take precedence over all other orders; refusal to comply may lead to seizure or other measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 9 — broad wartime procurement powers to ensure supply of arms/ammunition and necessary equipment; Secretary of War/Navy may determine capability and necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seizure and use of manufacturing plants for war production
rubrics_metrics.description: When necessary, the appropriate branch of the Army or Navy is authorized to take immediate possession of any plant and manufacture therein such product or material as required; compensation for use shall be fair and just.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 9 and later text — temporary government possession of plants for war production with fair compensation; penalties for refusal to comply with preference orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for refusal to comply with manufacturing orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual, firm, association, company or corporation failing to comply with orders or refusing to manufacture ordered kinds, quantities or qualities, or refusing to give the United States preference, shall be guilty of a felony and upon conviction punished by imprisonment not more than three years and a fine not exceeding $50,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 9 (and related) — criminal penalties for noncompliance with obligatory orders for defense production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential power to prescribe rules, create selective service system and local boards
rubrics_metrics.description: The President may prescribe rules and regulations to carry out the act, create and establish a selective service system, provide for classification of registrants and volunteers on the basis of availability, and establish civilian local boards and other agencies including appeal boards as necessary to carry out the provisions of this act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 10(A)(1)-(2) — empowers President to set the regulatory framework and administrative apparatus for the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local board composition, appointment, residency and disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be one or more local boards in each county or political subdivision; each local board shall consist of three or more members appointed by the President from recommendations, each member shall be a civilian who is a citizen of the United States residing in the county or political subdivision, and no member shall be a member of the land or naval forces of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 10(A)(2) — local board membership rules, appointment sources and residency/jurisdiction requirements; subject to Presidential rules/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local boards' jurisdiction and finality of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Local boards, under Presidential rules and regulations, shall have power within their jurisdictions to hear and determine questions or claims with respect to inclusion for, or exemption or deferment from, training and service; decisions of such local boards shall be final except where an appeal is authorized under Presidential rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 10(A) — local boards are first-instance decision-makers; appeals provided only as prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on registration or deferment exception for selective service personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: No officer, member, agent or employee of the selective service system, or of any local or appeal board or other agency, shall be excepted from registration or deferment by reason of his status as such officer, member, agent or employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 10(A) — personnel of the system remain subject to registration and requirements unless otherwise provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and compensation of director and employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The President shall appoint, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, a director of selective service at compensation not in excess of $10,000 per annum and appoint other officers, agents and employees as necessary; clerical and stenographic employees for local boards may be appointed without regard to civil service classification laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 10(A)(3) — establishes director role, pay cap, and hiring flexibilities to staff the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilization of government and state services
rubrics_metrics.description: The President may utilize the services of any and all departments and officers or agents of the United States and accept the services of officers and agents of the several states, territories and the District of Columbia and subdivisions thereof in the execution of this act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 10(A)(4) — intergovernmental cooperation authorized to execute the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of Presidential authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is authorized, under such rules and regulations as he may prescribe, to delegate any authority vested in him under this act to officers, agents or persons he designates for such purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 10(B) — delegation permitted for operational administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of voluntary services and official correspondence privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary services may be accepted in the execution of this act and necessary correspondence may be carried in official penalty envelopes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 10(C) — administrative conveniences for carrying out the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal agent designation for selective service disbursements
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief of finance, United States Army, is designated to act as the fiscal, disbursing and accounting agent of the director of selective service in carrying out the provisions of this act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 10(D) — fiscal responsibilities assigned to Army finance chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal penalties for willful failures and falsifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person charged with duties under this act who knowingly fails or neglects to perform such duty, or knowingly makes or is a party to false or incorrect registration, classification, examination, deferment, induction, enrollment or related false statements, or who evades registration or service or counsels others to do so, or who hinders administration by force or violence, shall upon conviction be punished by imprisonment for not more than five years or a fine of not more than $10,000, or both; may be tried by court martial if subject to military law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 11 — broad criminal sanctions cover administrative personnel and registrants alike for fraudulent/obstructive conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlisted men's base pay schedule and specialist ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly base pay for enlisted men of the Army and Marine Corps is set by grade (first grade $126; second $84; third $72; fourth $60; fifth $54; sixth $36; seventh $30; with exceptions for new recruits/inefficiency); pay for specialists ratings (first class $30; second $25; third $20; fourth $15; fifth $6; sixth $3) and permanent percentage increases after service milestones (10% after first four years; additional 5% per four years up to 25% total); Navy pay parity required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 12(A)-(F) — prescribes base pay, specialist differentials, longevity increases (caps), parity for Navy, inclusion in retirement computation, effective dates and no retroactive back pay prior to Oct 1, 1940.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension and modification of Soldiers' and Sailors' Civil Relief Act benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits of the Soldiers and Sailors Civil Relief Act (March 8, 1918) are extended to all persons inducted and on active duty for more than one month, with certain provisions rendered inoperative and definitions adjusted (e.g., 'persons in military service', 'period of military service', and 'date of approval' deemed to mean enactment date of this Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 13 — specifies which prior statutory provisions remain operative and how key terms are to be construed for those inducted under this Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of requirements by publication of registration times
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person shall be deemed to have notice of the requirements of this act upon publishing a time for any registration under Section 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 14(A) — constructive notice via official publication of registration times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability and appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: If any provision of this act is held invalid, the remainder shall not be affected (severability). There are authorized appropriations out of the Treasury as necessary to carry out the provisions of this act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sec. 14(B)-(C) — standard severability clause and authorization of necessary funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate effect and short title
rubrics_metrics.description: This act shall take effect immediately and may be cited as the 'Selective Training and Service Act of 1940.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secs. 17-18 — effective date and official citation of the Act.
